Algebra I · Lesson 4.3

Variables on Both Sides

Solve this lesson →All lessons

In 4.1 a check proved that y=6y=6 solves 4y−7=2y+54y−7=2y+5. The check never produced the 66, though, and 4.2's moves only reached equations with the variable on one side. One observation closes the gap. Once the variable has a value, a term like 2y2y is a number, and 4.2 already lets you subtract any number from both sides.

Problem
The equation 8k=5k+218k=5k+21 has its variable on both sides, which 4.2 never faced. At the solution, though, 5k5k is a number like any other. Subtract 5k5k from both sides, finish with 4.2's moves, and check in the original. Enter the solution.
Show a hint
  • The balance move from 4.2 subtracts equal amounts from both sides, and the amount subtracted is allowed to contain the variable.
  • Subtracting 5k5k from both sides leaves 3k=213k=21.
Show the full solution
Subtract 5k5k from both sides, 3k=213k=21, then divide by 33, k=7k=7​. Check, 8⋅7=568⋅7=56 and 5⋅7+21=565⋅7+21=56. Subtracting 5k5k is a valid balance move because at the solution 5k5k stands for a single number.
Key idea
Collect the variable terms. At a solution, a variable term such as 5k5k is a number, so subtracting it from both sides is 4.2's balance move, and adding it back reverses the move, so the two equations are equivalent. The consequence is that one subtraction turns any equation with the variable on both sides into an equation with the variable on one side, and 4.2's moves finish those. Collecting the variable terms onto one side is the one new skill of this lesson.
Problem
Solve 9m+16=4m+619m+16=4m+61. Collect the variable terms with one subtraction, then unwind the 4.2 way. Check in the original before entering the solution.
Show a hint
  • Which single subtraction leaves the variable on only one side of the equation?
  • Subtracting 4m4m from both sides gives 5m+16=615m+16=61.
Show the full solution
Subtract 4m4m, 5m+16=615m+16=61, subtract 1616, 5m=455m=45, divide by 55, m=9m=9​. Check, 9⋅9+16=979⋅9+16=97 and 4⋅9+61=974⋅9+61=97.
Problem
Solve 2y+59=7y+192y+59=7y+19 twice. First subtract 2y2y from both sides and finish. Then start over and subtract 7y7y instead, letting the coefficient go negative along the way. Enter the value both routes give.
Show a hint
  • Both routes are legal. One subtracts 2y2y from both sides, the other subtracts 7y7y.
  • Route one gives 59=5y+1959=5y+19. Route two gives −5y+59=19−5y+59=19.
Show the full solution
Route one, subtract 2y2y, 59=5y+1959=5y+19, so 5y=405y=40 and y=8y=8. Route two, subtract 7y7y, −5y+59=19−5y+59=19, so −5y=−40−5y=−40 and y=8y=8 again. Either way y=8y=8​, and both sides check to 7575. Subtracting the smaller variable term keeps the coefficient positive, which is the friendlier road.
Key idea
Subtract the smaller variable term. Both routes are legal balance moves and land on the same solution, so pick the arithmetic you prefer. Removing the smaller variable term keeps the surviving coefficient positive, so no dividing by negatives later. Sometimes the variable then collects on the right side, which is fine, since 4.1 says the sides of an equation can trade places. And a subtracted variable term, like the 4x4x in 9−4x9−4x, is removed by adding it to both sides, the same principle run in reverse.
Problem
Solve 4a+57=12a+94a+57=12a+9. The smaller variable term is on the left this time, so subtracting it collects the variable on the right. Enter the solution.
Show a hint
  • Subtracting the smaller variable term keeps the remaining coefficient positive.
  • Subtracting 4a4a from both sides gives 57=8a+957=8a+9.
Show the full solution
Subtract 4a4a, 57=8a+957=8a+9, subtract 99, 8a=488a=48, so a=6a=6​. Check, 4⋅6+57=814⋅6+57=81 and 12⋅6+9=8112⋅6+9=81. A variable on the right is no problem, you can swap the two sides of an equation whenever you like.

Some equations need cleanup before anything crosses the equals sign. If a side is a pile of like terms, combine them the 2.4 way, and if parentheses are in the way, distribute once the 2.1 way. Simplifying a side rewrites it as an equal expression, so nothing on the other side changes. Collect once the sides are clean.

Problem
Solve 9g+8−2g+7=3g+359g+8−2g+7=3g+35. Combine like terms on the left the 2.4 way before collecting anything across the equals sign. Enter the solution.
Show a hint
  • Clean each side first. Balance moves come after the sides are simplified.
  • The left side combines to 7g+157g+15.
Show the full solution
The left side combines to 7g+157g+15, so 7g+15=3g+357g+15=3g+35. Subtract 3g3g, 4g+15=354g+15=35, so 4g=204g=20 and g=5g=5​. Check, 45+8−10+7=5045+8−10+7=50 and 3⋅5+35=503⋅5+35=50.
Problem
Solve 7(w−2)=4w+227(w−2)=4w+22. Distribute once the 2.1 way, then collect the variable terms. Enter the solution. Check in the original before entering it.
Show a hint
  • Parentheses come off before any term moves across the equals sign.
  • Distributing gives 7w−14=4w+227w−14=4w+22.
Show the full solution
Distribute, 7w−14=4w+227w−14=4w+22. Subtract 4w4w, 3w−14=223w−14=22, add 1414, 3w=363w=36, so w=12w=12​. Check, 7(12−2)=707(12−2)=70 and 4⋅12+22=704⋅12+22=70.

Negative and fraction solutions were normal outcomes in 4.2, and they stay normal here. Collecting the variable terms changes where the variable sits, not what kind of number the answer is allowed to be, so run the same moves and let the value be whatever it is.

Problem
Solve 5−6x=4x+255−6x=4x+25. The variable term on the left is subtracted, so adding 6x6x to both sides removes it. Enter the solution.
Show a hint
  • A subtracted term is removed by adding it to both sides, the same balance principle.
  • Adding 6x6x to both sides gives 5=10x+255=10x+25.
Show the full solution
Add 6x6x to both sides, 5=10x+255=10x+25, subtract 2525, 10x=−2010x=−20, so x=−2x=−2​. Check, 5−6(−2)=175−6(−2)=17 and 4(−2)+25=174(−2)+25=17. Negative solutions are ordinary outcomes here, exactly as in 4.2.
Problem
Solve 5x+2=2x+45x+2=2x+4. Nothing about collecting requires a whole-number answer. Enter the solution as a fraction in lowest terms.
Show a hint
  • Collect first, then divide at the end, and keep the result exact.
  • Subtracting 2x2x and then 22 leaves 3x=23x=2.
Show the full solution
Subtract 2x2x, 3x+2=43x+2=4, then subtract 22, 3x=23x=2, and divide by 33, x=23x=32​​. Check, both sides come out 163316​. A fractional solution is a normal outcome, and exact fractions keep the check honest.
Key idea
When the variable disappears. Collecting can cancel every variable term, and the number statement left behind settles everything. A false statement such as 4=94=9 means no solutions, the claim fails at every value. A true statement means every value is a solution and the equation is an identity, because by 2.1 the two sides were the same expression all along. Watch for the lookalike. If a variable term remains, as in 3x=03x=0, nothing special happened, and the equation has the one ordinary solution x=0x=0.
Problem
Solve 5(4x+3)=20x+85(4x+3)=20x+8. Distribute, then try to collect. The variable cancels entirely and a number statement is left behind. Decide whether that statement is true, then enter how many solutions the equation has.
Show a hint
  • When every variable term cancels, the leftover statement answers the question by itself.
  • Distributing gives 20x+15=20x+820x+15=20x+8.
Show the full solution
Distribute, 20x+15=20x+820x+15=20x+8. Subtracting 20x20x from both sides leaves 15=815=8, which is false, so the equation has 00​ solutions. The left side is always 77 more than the right, and no value of xx closes that gap.
Problem
Solve 13x+18−6x=7x+1813x+18−6x=7x+18. Combine the left side, then try to collect. The variable cancels and a true statement remains. Enter how many of the values −7−7, 00, 55, 1515 are solutions.
Show a hint
  • A true leftover statement means the two sides were the same expression all along.
  • The left side combines to 7x+187x+18, identical to the right side.
Show the full solution
The left side combines to 7x+187x+18, so the equation reads 7x+18=7x+187x+18=7x+18, true at every value, and all 44​ of the listed values are solutions. An equation whose two sides are equivalent expressions, like this one, is called an identity, and every value of xx satisfies it.
Problem
Solve 11x−4=6x−411x−4=6x−4. It looks like the last two problems and is neither one. Collect the variable terms, finish the 4.2 way, and check your value in the original before entering the solution.
Show a hint
  • Did the variable actually cancel, or is a variable term still there after the collecting?
  • Subtracting 6x6x from both sides gives 5x−4=−45x−4=−4, so 5x=05x=0.
Show the full solution
Subtract 6x6x, 5x−4=−45x−4=−4, add 44, 5x=05x=0, so x=0x=0​. Check, 11⋅0−4=−411⋅0−4=−4 and 6⋅0−4=−46⋅0−4=−4. Having the solution 00 is not the same as having 00 solutions, one value works and that value happens to be zero.
Fun fact
Al-jabr was only half the title. Al-Khwarizmi's book taught hisab al-jabr wa'l-muqabala, calculation by restoring and balancing, and the balancing, al-muqabala, is this lesson's move, removing equal amounts from the two sides of an equation.

A check belongs to the original equation. Substituting a candidate into one of your own later lines only tests the work that came after that line, and a line with a mistake in it will confirm an answer carrying the same mistake. The original equation is the claim you set out to solve, so the original is where a check means something.

Problem
A student solves 7x+44=3x+87x+44=3x+8, subtracting 3x3x and then 4444, but writes 4x=364x=36 instead of 4x=−364x=−36 and gets x=9x=9. Checking against the line 4x=364x=36 passes. Run the check where it counts. Substitute x=9x=9 into both sides of the original equation and enter how much larger the left side is than the right.
Show a hint
  • A check against a derived line only confirms that line, not the original equation.
  • At x=9x=9 the left side is 63+4463+44.
Show the full solution
At x=9x=9 the left side is 7⋅9+44=1077⋅9+44=107 and the right side is 3⋅9+8=353⋅9+8=35, so the left side is larger by 107−35=72107−35=72​. The correct line is 4x=−364x=−36, so x=−9x=−9, and both sides of the original then equal −19−19. A check against 4x=364x=36 tested the wrong claim.

One subtraction turns a both-sides equation into a one-side equation, and a variable that cancels is an answer rather than a failure, either no solutions or all of them. 4.4 takes on equations that hide this shape behind fractions and heavier parentheses, and 4.5 puts equations to work on word problems.

Practice these ideas

Practice
Enter the solution of 6x+7=4x+156x+7=4x+15.
Show the solution
Subtract 4x4x, 2x+7=152x+7=15, then subtract 77, 2x=82x=8, so x=4x=4​. Check, both sides equal 3131.
Practice
Enter the solution of 10x+26=3x+8910x+26=3x+89.
Show the solution
Subtract 3x3x, 7x+26=897x+26=89, then subtract 2626, 7x=637x=63, so x=9x=9​. Check, both sides equal 116116.
Practice
Enter the solution of 4x+54=9x+44x+54=9x+4. The variable collects on the right, which is fine.
Show the solution
Subtract 4x4x from both sides, 54=5x+454=5x+4, so 5x=505x=50 and x=10x=10​. Check, 4(10)+54=944(10)+54=94 and 9(10)+4=949(10)+4=94. An equation reads the same in either direction, so a variable on the right needs no extra step.
Practice
Enter the solution of 6x+27=15x6x+27=15x.
Show the solution
Subtract 6x6x from both sides, 27=9x27=9x, so x=3x=3​. Check, 6(3)+27=456(3)+27=45 and 15(3)=4515(3)=45.
Practice
Enter the solution of 5x=3x+345x=3x+34.
Show the solution
Subtract 3x3x from both sides, 2x=342x=34, so x=17x=17​. Check, 5(17)=855(17)=85 and 3(17)+34=853(17)+34=85.
Practice
Enter the solution of 7x+41=2x+67x+41=2x+6.
Show the solution
Subtract 2x2x from both sides, 5x+41=65x+41=6, then 5x=−355x=−35 and x=−7x=−7​. Check, 7(−7)+41=−87(−7)+41=−8 and 2(−7)+6=−82(−7)+6=−8.
Practice
Combine like terms on the left first, then solve 8x−1+2x=7x+388x−1+2x=7x+38.
Show the solution
Combine first, 10x−1=7x+3810x−1=7x+38. Subtract 7x7x, 3x−1=383x−1=38, add 11, 3x=393x=39, so x=13x=13​. Check, both sides equal 129129.
Practice
Distribute first, then solve 4(2x−5)=6x+24(2x−5)=6x+2.
Show the solution
Distribute, 8x−20=6x+28x−20=6x+2. Subtract 6x6x, 2x−20=22x−20=2, then 2x=222x=22 and x=11x=11​. Check, 4(2⋅11−5)=4⋅17=684(2⋅11−5)=4⋅17=68 and 6(11)+2=686(11)+2=68.
Practice
Solve 6x+3=2x+176x+3=2x+17. Enter the solution as a fraction in lowest terms.
Show the solution
Subtract 2x2x, 4x+3=174x+3=17, then 4x=144x=14 and x=144=72x=414​=27​​. Check, 6⋅72+3=246⋅27​+3=24 and 2⋅72+17=242⋅27​+17=24.
Practice
Enter the solution of 48−3x=4x+648−3x=4x+6. Adding 3x3x to both sides is the collect move.
Show the solution
Add 3x3x to both sides, 48=7x+648=7x+6, then 7x=427x=42 and x=6x=6​. Check, 48−3(6)=3048−3(6)=30 and 4(6)+6=304(6)+6=30.
Practice
How many solutions does 6x+37=6x+506x+37=6x+50 have? Enter the count.
Show the solution
Subtracting 6x6x from both sides leaves 37=5037=50, which is false, so the equation has 00​ solutions. Whatever xx is, the two sides differ by 1313, so no value can ever make them equal.
Practice
How many of the values −8−8, −1−1, 00, 66, 2020 are solutions of 7(2x+8)=9x+5x+567(2x+8)=9x+5x+56?
Show the solution
Distributing gives 14x+5614x+56 on the left, and the right combines to 14x+5614x+56 as well, so the equation is an identity and every value works. All 55​ listed values are solutions. By 2.1 the two sides are equivalent expressions, so no substitution was ever needed.
Practice
Solve 7x+5=3x+57x+5=3x+5. Enter the solution.
Show the solution
Subtract 3x3x, 4x+5=54x+5=5, then subtract 55, 4x=04x=0, so x=0x=0​. Check, both sides equal 55. Zero is a legitimate solution, an equation whose sides agree only at 00 is nothing like an identity.
Practice
Solve 5x+1=9x+65x+1=9x+6. Enter the solution as a fraction in lowest terms.
Show the solution
Subtract 5x5x, 1=4x+61=4x+6, then 4x=−54x=−5 and x=−54x=−45​​. Check, 5(−54)+1=−2145(−45​)+1=−421​ and 9(−54)+6=−2149(−45​)+6=−421​. A negative solution changes nothing about the steps, collect the variable terms on one side and divide as usual.
Practice
A student solves 9x−7=2x+429x−7=2x+42 and gets x=3x=3. Substitute x=3x=3 into both sides of the original and enter how much larger the right side is than the left.
Show the solution
At x=3x=3 the left side is 9(3)−7=209(3)−7=20 and the right side is 2(3)+42=482(3)+42=48, so the right side is larger by 48−20=2848−20=28​. The correct run is 7x=497x=49, so x=7x=7, where both sides equal 5656.
Practice
Solve 2(6x+7)=5(2x+9)2(6x+7)=5(2x+9), one distribute on each side. Enter the solution as a fraction in lowest terms.
Show the solution
Distribute on both sides, 12x+14=10x+4512x+14=10x+45. Subtract 10x10x, 2x+14=452x+14=45, then 2x=312x=31 and x=312x=231​​. Check, 2(6⋅312+7)=2(100)=2002(6⋅231​+7)=2(100)=200 and 5(2⋅312+9)=5(40)=2005(2⋅231​+9)=5(40)=200.
Practice
Simplify both sides first, then solve 9−2x+8=4x−1+2x9−2x+8=4x−1+2x. Enter the solution as a fraction in lowest terms.
Show the solution
The left combines to 17−2x17−2x and the right to 6x−16x−1. Add 2x2x to both sides, 17=8x−117=8x−1, then 8x=188x=18 and x=188=94x=818​=49​​. Check, 9−2⋅94+8=2529−2⋅49​+8=225​ and 4⋅94−1+2⋅94=2524⋅49​−1+2⋅49​=225​.
